summary.headline: Muthoot Capital Q2 FY27: AUM crossed ₹3,530 crore (+25% YoY) and forward flow to NPA fell to 0.50%, while GNPA stood at 4.61%.
summary.overview: Management described H1 as a consolidation period, highlighting a rating upgrade to AA that allows pan-India fixed deposit mobilisation beyond Kerala. Disbursements grew about 21% in H1, with commercial vehicle, construction equipment and used car disbursements up over 100%. Co-lending and direct assignment exposure was wound down, cutting the co-lending book by about 52% to ₹382 crore, and the business is now sourced fully in-house for the first time in 48 months. Net interest income rose QoQ but the blended yield and cost of funds trends are still working through the book, and CFO flagged that Q2 impairment (₹21.44 crore) was below plan.

financial_highlights.change: Q1 and last-year comparisons not cleanly stated; last-year apples-to-apples cited as 5.76%
vs 0.85-0.87% last year and 0.67% in Q1
vs ₹77.66 crore in same quarter last year; ~₹80.46 crore excluding ~₹14 crore upfront DA interest
bank loans ₹200 crore, NCDs ₹400 crore, PTC/securitisation ₹353 crore, FD ₹85 crore

segments.name: Two-wheeler
segments.commentary: Core 'war horse' with ₹2,636 crore book; management cited approval rates rising from 45-50% to 70-75% after in-house scorecards, and yield at about 22% versus ~21.5% internal MCSL yield. Market share about 2.5-3%.

segments.name: Commercial vehicle / construction equipment
segments.commentary: Disbursements up over 100% in H1; book of ₹356 crore with GNPA 0.35%. Management says the segment is still in investment phase and not standalone profitable, with breakeven expected by end of this year.

segments.name: Used car
segments.commentary: Disbursements up over 100% in H1 off a small base; book of ₹215 crore with GNPA 1.31%. Breakeven expected in Q1 FY28.

segments.name: Co-lending / direct assignment
segments.commentary: Being wound down: book cut to ₹382 crore (-52%), with the last active partner closed in Q1. Lower-yielding book expected to fall toward ~₹200 crore over the next few quarters.

guidance_outlook: Expected monthly disbursement of ₹400+ crore from November onward; October was ₹306 crore.
Bank borrowing cost expected to fall by a further ~0.10% on next sanctions; target is each new bank tranche priced below the previous one.
Impairment to be kept well below 2% in the long run; management said it will not add a 0.56% overhead, though no firm quarterly number was given.
Long-term goal of ~4% ROA, with the company stating it stands by that target; a 4.5% blended ROA was referenced earlier.
BRE and scorecards for two-wheeler to be fully in-house by December.
Management expects NII growth in FY28 to outpace FY27 as lower-yield co-lending book runs off.
capex_capacity: Pan-India fixed deposit campaign launched after AA rating upgrade, replacing the earlier Kerala-only restriction.
Online FD platform and video KYC launched earlier this year; deposit book grew about 250% YoY.
In-house BRE and scorecard development moved from vendors to internal data science team; change cycle reduced from vendor request to internal control.
Account aggregator usage: about 40-45% of two-wheeler hits and over 65% of car and CV hits.
demand_pricing: Two-wheeler approval rates lifted from 45-50% to 70-75%, driving market share gains in recent months.
Industry retail vehicle sales in October 2026 were reportedly down ~32% YoY (about 20 lakh units vs 30 lakh), partly due to festive timing shifts.
Management plans to grow CV and used car to about 60% of the book over two years, with two-wheeler at 36% per the mix discussed.
Bank funding cost market is not expected to ease much beyond the rating-driven savings already achieved.
ARC recoveries from the Phoenix pool were about ₹225 crore over the last 6-7 months; management expects ARC1 to reach 80-85% of repayments next year.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving retail book growth and market share gains?
qa_highlights.answer: Management credited a new in-house origination scorecard that lifted approval rates to 70-75% from 45-50%. October industry retail was about 32% lower YoY due to festive timing, but MCSL's October disbursement hit ₹306 crore, a record.

qa_highlights.question: How will public deposits grow and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: The AA rating enables pan-India FD mobilisation; the online platform and video KYC have widened access. Management says FD rates are better than peers and the cost is below current borrowing costs.

qa_highlights.question: Why is NII not growing in line with AUM?
qa_highlights.answer: Q2 NII of ₹94.46 crore included ~₹14 crore upfront DA interest; excluding it, ~₹80.46 crore, still ~11-12% above last year. Repayments dilute net growth, and low-yield co-lending (~25% of book in Q2 last year, now near zero) weighs on blended yield, which is expected to rise over 2-3 quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Will the gross/net yield and cost structure allow the 4% ROA target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated the ~4% ROA goal. Used car and CV are loss-making in investment phase, with breakeven expected by end of this year (CV) and Q1 FY28 (used car), while IT spend weighs; the two-wheeler business is carrying the earnings.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company using account aggregators and would it rely more on AA data?
qa_highlights.answer: AA is already used for about a year: roughly 40-45% of two-wheeler hits and over 65% for car and CV, which management called above industry levels.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for Phoenix ARC recoveries and where will growth come from geographically?
qa_highlights.answer: Phoenix pool recoveries run around ₹225 crore over 6-7 months against a ₹102 crore security receipt balance, with recovery expected by September next year. Growth will come from deepening existing states rather than new geographies, with two-wheeler share at 2.5-3%.

risks_watch: GNPA at 4.61% and NNPA at 2.75% with PCR flat at 50%; watch recoveries from legacy NPA pools.
Margin pressure from low-yield co-lending run-off and the timing of yield recovery; NII growth lagged AUM growth in Q2.
Cash burn in used car and CV businesses until breakeven targets (CV end-2026, used car Q1 FY28) are met.
Bank funding cost reduction is expected to be modest (~0.10%) given tight market conditions.
Festive-season volume and ability to sustain ₹400 crore+ monthly disbursements from November.
Pan-India FD ramp-up and its effect on liability cost and the deposit book.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth, asset quality trend and funding diversification, with specific numbers offered throughout. More cautious on near-term margins and profitability, where management acknowledged the ROA target is some distance away and new businesses still burn cash.
key_quotes: We don't intend to pursue growth at the expense of asset quality.
And the most heartening part is that our forward flow to NPA was the last year same time.
So in the last year we had a forward flow of about 0.78% which has come down to 0.5%, which is a very, very significant improvement.
This is the first quarter in last 48 months wherein the company has sourced the entire business through its MCSL only.

growth.why: Management guides monthly disbursement of ₹400+ crore from November (vs ₹306 crore in October) and expects NII growth in FY28 to outpace FY27, backed by two-wheeler approval rates lifting to 70-75%, pan-India FD mobilisation after the AA upgrade and co-lending run-off, but no capacity additions or firm revenue growth number were given.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Blended yield expected to rise over 2-3 quarters as low-yield co-lending (~25% of book last year, now near zero; book down 52% to ₹382 crore) runs off, and bank borrowing cost is guided down ~0.10% on next sanctions, though management is cautious on near-term profitability with ROA (PAT) at 0.75%.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No new plants, lines or branches were guided; growth is coming from deepening existing states and pan-India FD mobilisation, not new capacity.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guides monthly disbursement of ₹400+ crore from November vs ₹306 crore in October (a record), backed by two-wheeler approval rates lifting from 45-50% to 70-75%.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex is not discussed; with no capacity build-out cited and the business asset-light (lending book), there is no utilisation-driven trigger for a capex announcement.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management expects FY28 NII growth to outpace FY27 and reiterated a ~4% long-term ROA goal, but no revised numeric guidance was given and Q2 NII (₹94.46 crore incl. ~₹14 crore upfront DA interest) lagged AUM growth of 25%.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: GNPA at 4.61% with PCR flat at 50%, used car and CV still loss-making until breakeven targets (CV end-2026, used car Q1 FY28), and bank funding cost cuts limited to ~0.10% as market tightness persists.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Used car and CV/construction equipment are scaling (disbursements up over 100% in H1, books ₹215 crore and ₹356 crore), and pan-India FD products are rolling out, but no specific new product launch date was named.

rows.label: Bank borrowing cost cut of ~0.10% on next sanctions
rows.why: Management expects another ~0.10% reduction on next bank tranches, with each new tranche targeted below the previous one, after the AA rating upgrade.

rows.label: Cheaper liability mix via pan-India FDs
rows.why: Public deposit book at ₹155 crore (~250% YoY) with management saying FD cost is below current borrowing costs of 9.52%, and pan-India FD mobilisation now permitted after the AA upgrade.

rows.label: Used car and CV breakeven
rows.why: CV and construction equipment book ₹356 crore (GNPA 0.35%) targets breakeven by end-2026 and used car book ₹215 crore targets breakeven in Q1 FY28; both still loss-making today.

tone.note: Management was confident on disbursement momentum, asset quality trend and funding diversification with specific numbers, but cautious on near-term margins and the ~4% ROA target, which it acknowledged is some distance away; analysts pushed on why NII lagged AUM growth and the cash burn in used car
